newsitem.title: UK: NZ SPORT-RUGBY UNION-English media praise NZ Barbarians.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-RUGBY UNION-English media praise NZ Barbarians.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 1 - English rugby journalists were sent reaching for their dictionaries to find words to describe the New Zealand Barbarians after their 34-19 win over England at Twickenham, NZPA reported on Monday (NZT).
"Kiwi Aura Dazzles England" said the Observer, with writer Mick Cleary saying the class of the New Zealanders was the decisive factor.
Former England lock Paul Ackford, writing in the Sunday Telegraph, could only say: "Staggering, simply staggering".
And in the Mail on Sunday, Malcolm Folley wrote that the Barbarians proved to England that southern hemisphere rugby had "edged somewhere over the horizon from the game we are accustomed to seeing".

Fullback Christian Cullen and replacement first five-eighth Carlos Spencer were picked out as the players with the biggest individual impact on the game, but the overall superiority of the Barbarians was commented on by all papers.

Under the headline "Baa-Baa Blacks fleece England", Sunday Times writer Stephen Jones said: "Due homage to a New Zealand Barbarians team that outclassed England in every phase of this match, so utterly that it was embarrassing.

"New Zealand should be given heartfelt thanks by everyone with rugby in their soul. They have proved that professional rugby can work brilliantly....They are undoubtedly the best side in the world this season."
If the Barbarians had taken their kicks, rather than running penalties, a score of 50 or 60 points would not have been a distortion, he said.
Against the "dazzling" New Zealanders, Jones added, England were made to look "grafting and pedestrian".
Ackford, in the Sunday Telegraph, praised England for competing with the Barbarians for most of the match, and said several younger players "came of age".
"But for all England's achievements it was New Zealand who stole the show and proved conclusively that they have no peer in world rugby," he said.
"It was not an All Black test side, nor did they play with the intensity of one, but they still had the vision, pace and ruggedness to win a titanically tight contest."
In the process, Ackford added, the Barbarians "unearthed another monumental talent called Carlos Spencer".
In the Observer, Cleary wrote that New Zealand's all-round superiority finally won through.
"There was a compelling sense of their greater athleticism, awareness, drive, skill and, crucially, pace.
"There was more crackle and energy to the Barbarians play all over the field. The style, grace and penetrating incursions of Christian Cullen, the 20-year-old fullback, took the breath away."

Writing in the Mail on Sunday, former England captain Will Carling said it would be virtually impossible for England to compete against the best regularly unless there was a radical restructure of the English game.
